name: Long exposure night
means: One frame integrated over many seconds: moving lights drawn as continuous ribbons, water and cloud smeared to smooth milk, static architecture pin sharp, every light source blown out into flare.
prose: a long exposure night photograph, thirty seconds on a tripod, car headlights and tail lights drawn as continuous unbroken ribbons of white and red, water smoothed to milk, static architecture perfectly sharp, streetlights blown out into starburst flare
negative_add: handheld, blurred subject, daylight, flat lighting, illustration, anime
works_for: video: it cannot survive, and not because of a model weakness. A long exposure IS a single frame integrated over time, so animating it is a contradiction - LTX will slide the light trails around as though they were solid objects. If a shot needs this look, hold on the still. Reasoned from what the style is, not measured.
note: Read the two halves separately, because only one of them belongs here. The LIGHT TRAILS are real nouns and land on qwen - PROMPTING.md lists `long exposure` among the photographic vocabulary that works. The DARKNESS does not come from this card at all: studio/looks/night.json holds the measurement, `night, dark background` moved mean luma 170 to 161, i.e. nothing. Author the trails as a style and get the dark from the night or moonlit GRADE, which is deterministic and exact. This is the single most common place in the set where a style gets mistaken for a look. Unavailable on the anime checkpoint - and note motion blur lives in that model's negative, not its positive. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
verdict: Genuine light trails from traffic. Unambiguous.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject. studio/_tools/style_examples.py
